text: This video replays Leah's illustrative loan through every ten-year stretch of U.S. interest rates since January nineteen fifty-four. Each replay moves her rate up and down exactly as much as the three-month Treasury bill rate moved in that stretch of history, and the data is U.S. only. "Worth it" gets one plain meaning here: how often the variable loan cost more in total interest than the nine percent fixed loan, and how much more at worst. Then the replay moves the head start, from three points down to a variable rate starting one point above the fixed one, to see where that history changes. By the end there's a line that any real offer can be held up against, including yours. This is history, not a forecast.
